interface.title: CD40 Immunosome: A Systems Biology Framework (CD40 Immunosome Tool, Streamlit)
interface.field: Immunology / systems biology (CD40–TRAF6–NF-κB–SOCS1 signalling, immunotherapy target prioritization)
interface.stage_of_work: Hypothesis generation before wet-lab work: in-silico kinetic modelling, sensitivity and robustness checks, knockout target ranking
interface.what_it_is_for: Simulating CD40-driven NF-κB dynamics with SOCS1 negative feedback from adjustable rate constants, comparing it with a no-feedback model, stress-testing it with Monte Carlo parameter noise, and ranking CRISPR knockout targets by AUC-based synergy.

data.note: Nothing is uploaded. All model outputs come from the built-in RK4 ODE model driven by the sidebar sliders (k1, k2, k3, k4, k6, k7, k8, CD40 input). The two dropdowns (delivery vehicle, CD40 agonist) do not enter the ODE, synergy or Monte Carlo calculations. They change only the Immunosome Builder metric cards and the network and table labels. The Dark Proteome table, Molecular Validation affinity table, cell-type bar chart and supplementary concept ranking are fixed demo tables. The exported TXT summary was read back twice. The first matched the Gold NP / Selicrelumab / k6=0.50 settings. The second matched CP-870,893 / k1=0.20 / k4=0.10 / k6=0.00 / CD40=2.00.

tree.general: Build and stress-test a mechanistic model of a feedback-regulated signalling pathway to generate testable hypotheses
tree.specific: Model CD40→TRAF6→NF-κB with SOCS1 feedback, check its behaviour without feedback and under parameter noise, and rank CRISPR knockouts that boost NF-κB output

features.name: Seeded Monte Carlo robustness test
features.general: Perturb all parameters randomly within ±20%, re-simulate N times, and summarize the spread of outcomes with a reproducible seed
features.specific: Monte Carlo seed box (−/+) and Run Monte Carlo Stress Test (n=50): mean ±1σ band, optional raw trajectories, Mean Peak NF-κB and Mean Time-to-Peak with SD, AUC histogram and verdict box. Caveats: the 'Robustness Confirmed: System maintains transient peak' verdict is unconditional and appeared even with no transient (t_peak 200.00 at k6=0). The last result stays on screen after parameter changes until you re-run. The seed resets to 42 when you switch views.

not_done: The CSV download from the CRISPR synergy table toolbar produced no file in the downloads list, so the synergy table could not be exported as CSV here.

There is no separate time-to-peak readout for a single deterministic run. Time-to-peak appears only as Baseline/KO t_peak in the CRISPR table and as Mean Time-to-Peak in the Monte Carlo summary. I estimated the single-run peak only by eye from the chart (screens/047.webp).
Vega tooltip text on chart hover was not captured in screenshots, except once while zoomed (screens/018.webp).

Not all dropdown options were tried: of the delivery vehicles only Liposome and Gold NP, and of the agonists only CD40L (Native), Selicrelumab and CP-870,893. Exosome, PLGA Polymer and Dacetuzumab were not tried. The replay did try Dacetuzumab.

Delivery vehicle and agonist do not reach the model. Vehicle changes only the Clustering Regime and Antigen Presentation Gain cards and the network label. Agonist changes only labels (network node, affinity-table row, TXT export). Neither enters the ODE, synergy or Monte Carlo calculations. The run saw agonist changes leave the synergy scores unchanged (screens/059.webp). The reviewer's reading of app.py confirms that SCAFFOLD_MODELS feeds only the metric cards and that simulate_signaling_ode takes no scaffold argument. So the README's question 1, whether scaffold clustering changes NF-κB dynamics, is not actually modelled by this tool.
The Monte Carlo verdict 'Robustness Confirmed: System maintains transient peak' still appeared when there was no transient peak (mean t_peak 200.00 with k6=0, screens/057.webp). It is fixed text.
The Monte Carlo seed went back to 42 after switching views, and the last Monte Carlo result stayed on screen after parameters changed until re-run (screens/055.webp).
